findings.text: Export register_kprobe registers one breakpoint probe. Contract accepts either a direct location or a symbolic name with displacement plus an optional start disabled request. Guarantees canonical location resolution, entry coincidence derivation, flag sanitization preserving only the disabled request, cleared miss accounting, text and reservation validation with temporary module hold, and insertion into the address hash with best effort arming and optimization attempt.

Export register_kprobes registers many breakpoint probes as a batch. Contract rejects non positive counts. Guarantees ordered registration and rollback of the already registered prefix when any element fails, returning the failure status of the failing element.

Exports unregister_kprobe and unregister_kprobes remove breakpoint probes. Contract uses two phases separated by a grace period. First phase detaches logically under the central mutex and marks failures with a null location. Second phase performs arch cleanup only for survivors. Single removal is defined as batch removal of length one.

Export static_call_text_reserved reports whether a queried address interval collides with any static call patch site. Contract covers both built in sites and module sites. Returns positive on collision and zero when free. Behaviour for module ownership is defined by the module aware helper variant.

Export kprobe_on_func_entry tests whether a described location coincides with function entry. Contract accepts direct or symbolic description with displacement. Reports success only when address resolution succeeds and the arch hook confirms entry coincidence, otherwise reports invalid argument or resolution failure.

Exports kretprobe_find_ret_addr and its cursor helper locate saved return locations for a task while skipping trampoline placeholders. Contract scans the per task instance chain from the start or from a supplied cursor, updates the cursor to the matching node, and filters by frame identity in the outer wrapper. Null cursor input is warned and yields zero.

Export kprobe_flush_task discards all pending return probe instances owned by a task. Contract is a no operation before subsystem initialization completes. Otherwise guarantees the per task chain is drained atomically from the task and every instance is recycled through the shared recycle path under a busy section.

Exports for supported return probing provide function entry return interception with batch forms. Supported registration requires entry coincidence, enforces blacklist and data size limits, establishes default capacity when unspecified, allocates per probe instance storage, then registers the underlying entry probe. Batch registration rolls back its prefix on failure. Batch unregistration detaches under the central mutex, releases or detaches instance storage, waits for grace, then performs bottom cleanup and pool teardown for survivors. Single forms delegate to batch forms.

Unsupported variants report or ignore return probe operations when the feature is disabled. Registration entry points report not supported. Unregistration entry points and the fallback entry interceptor perform no action and return no status where void.

Weak default hooks arch_adjust_kprobe_addr, arch_kretprobe_fixup_return and kprobe_exceptions_notify allow arch override. Default address adjustment treats zero displacement as entry and combines base with displacement. Default return fixup performs no action. Default exception notification reports no handling.

Canonical location resolution requires exactly one of direct address and symbolic name. Symbolic input is looked up with displacement, then displaced, rebased to symbol start through a size and offset query, and finally recombined by the arch hook which also reports entry coincidence. Invalid combinations, missing symbols, failed size queries and arch rejection are reported as distinct failures. A small wrapper resolves from probe fields and discards entry status.

Probe identity validation looks up the aggregate resident at the same location. Identity holds when the queried probe is the resident itself or a member of its child list, otherwise validation fails. Re registration detection warns once when validation succeeds and rejects with invalid argument.

Ftrace location handling marks a probe when its location coincides with an ftrace patch site. When ftrace based probing is enabled the probe gains the ftrace flag, otherwise such a location is rejected as invalid. Non ftrace locations pass unchanged.

Compiler integrity preamble detection resolves the symbol name for an address and reports a match when the name begins with either of two reserved prefixes for integrity and prefix trampolines. Lookup failure means no match.

Address safety requires ftrace clearance, then membership in core text or module text, and absence from gate areas, probe blacklist, jump label reservations, static call reservations, bug locations and integrity preambles. Module targets need a successful reference hold during patching, and init text of a non coming module is rejected as missing. Every rejection releases any module reference already taken.

Static call collision detection decodes each site key and instruction location as a self relative sum, tests an init marker bit in the decoded key, and reports overlap when the fixed size call instruction at the site intersects the queried interval. Init sites are skipped once the system or module has left the coming phase, otherwise all sites are examined.

Module aware static call scan locates the module owning the interval start under read protection, warns when interval end belongs elsewhere, holds a module reference for the scan, evaluates that module site array with coming state awareness, then releases the reference. Absent module or failed hold means no collision. The no module build always reports no collision.

Internal registration distinguishes collision from fresh insertion. When a resident already occupies the location the request is delegated to aggregate registration. Otherwise preparation occurs under text exclusion, the node is inserted into the address hash for deferred readers, arming occurs unless globally disarmed or individually disabled with removal and grace on arm failure, followed by a best effort optimization attempt.

Disable semantics separate child state from aggregate state. An aggregate counts as disabled only when every child is disabled. Disabling an already disabled probe is idempotent. Child disable marks the child, then disarms and marks the aggregate only when the target is the aggregate itself or all children became disabled. Disarm failure restores the child mark and reports the error.

Unregistration top phase disables first, then either removes the aggregate from the hash when independent or last disarmed child, or detaches the child from the aggregate list. When the departing child provided post handling and no survivor does, aggregate post handling is cleared except for the ftrace case which retains it as an arming marker, followed by re optimization when still enabled. Bottom phase dispatches on list shape to arch removal, last child promotion with aggregate release, or no action for already detached children.

Supported return probe admission requires entry coincidence, duplicate detection when a direct address is given, absence from the return blacklist by resolved address, and bounded per instance data size. Capacity defaults to a scaled function of possible processor count with a floor when unspecified. Instance storage is allocated either as rethook backing or as pooled holder memory with zeroed miss accounting before underlying entry registration, and is released when that registration fails.

Return instance management binds each pooled object to its holder at creation, releases holder memory at teardown, and returns objects to the owning probe pool when the probe remains known. Orphaned objects are freed through a deferred callback that drops them to the holder pool. Holder teardown clears the probe back link and finalizes the pool when present.

Trampoline handling resolves the correct return for the current frame, treats absence as a fatal diagnostic, publishes the corrected location as the instruction pointer for tracing, invokes user handlers for every instance of the frame with per processor current probe tracking and return update, applies the arch fixup, then detaches the whole frame chain at once and recycles its instances.

Entry interception has pooled and rethook forms with shared miss and veto semantics. Both acquire an instance and count a miss when none is available. Both consult the optional entry filter and recycle immediately on veto. The pooled form prepares arch state and links to the current task chain. The rethook form hooks through the rethook layer with ftrace awareness. The rethook completion path validates its context, marks active status, and invokes the user return handler with current probe tracking.

Central probe mutex serializes identity validation, duplicate detection, registration, disable aggregation, and the top half of unregistration. Callers assert its ownership in validation, aggregation query and disable paths. Batch removal holds it across all top halves. Return probe batch teardown acquires it per element.

Text mutation exclusion combines processor read lock with text mutex around probe preparation. Reservation checks hold the jump label lock across text classification and veto tests, with deferred reclamation protection for module lookup. Hash and list removal use deferred reclamation, and callers wait for a grace period before arch cleanup, pool teardown or reuse of detached memory. Task flush uses a busy section around chain draining.

Observed breakpoint probe state includes a direct location, an optional symbolic name with displacement, flag bits for disabled start and derived entry and ftrace and aggregate and disarmed conditions, a miss counter, hash linkage keyed by location, child list linkage, and optional pre and post handlers. Aggregate residents own a child list used for membership and post handler inheritance.

Observed return probe state includes an embedded breakpoint probe, entry and return handlers, per instance data size, capacity, miss counter, and either a pooled holder with instance pool and back link or a rethook allocation. Observed instance state includes return location, frame identity, task list linkage, deferred free linkage, holder link or rethook node, and trailing user data area sized by the probe.

Observed static call site state includes a self relative key encoding an init marker and a self relative instruction location. Decoding adds the stored field to its own address. Observed exception notifier state binds a callback with a maximum priority requesting earliest delivery.

Breakpoint probe lifecycle moves from address canonicalization and duplicate rejection through safety validation to internal registration, then hash insertion, conditional arming, and optimization attempt. Disable moves through child marking to conditional aggregate disarm. Removal moves through disable and hash or list detachment under lock, grace wait, then arch cleanup or aggregate release.

Return instance lifecycle moves from pool or rethook acquisition through optional entry filter to task linkage or hook, then frame completion with user handler execution, followed by frame detachment and recycling. Misses return to entry without linkage. Task exit drains all owned instances through recycling. Unregistration detaches storage before grace and tears down pools after grace for survivors.

Static call reservation lifecycle distinguishes early from running phases. Built in scans treat system state before running as init inclusive and skip init sites afterwards. Module scans treat the coming state as init inclusive and skip init sites after arrival. The no module build remains in the always free state.

Entry points include earliest exception notification, trampoline completion for return frames, pooled and rethook entry interceptors, and rethook completion. The trampoline is explicitly excluded from probing. Entry interceptors run in probe context with task linkage. Completion paths run with current probe tracking and active status marking where applicable.

Fatal path triggers when trampoline completion finds no saved return, logging a diagnostic and halting. Warning paths cover duplicate registration, cross module interval queries, frame identity mismatch during completion, and null cursor queries. Warnings are once only where repeated triggering is likely.

Lifetime hazards include module unload during patching mitigated by temporary holds with release on every exit, use after detach mitigated by grace waits before bottom cleanup and pool teardown, double completion mitigated by nulling failed detach locations, and lost wakeups from disarmed or disabled states handled by conditional arming and best effort global operations.

Notifier ABI requests earliest delivery through the maximum signed priority value and signals no handling through the done decision code. Facts rest on the static notifier definition and the weak default callback.

ABI surface includes flag bits for disabled start, ftrace use, entry coincidence, aggregate and gone and disarmed states, a hit active status for rethook completion, a hash width for the address table, a symbol name length for preamble checks, a maximum return data size, and static call decoding with an init marker bit and fixed call size. Presence is observed, numeric encodings are not shown in these fragments.

Failure ABI uses invalid argument for bad combinations and vetoed or non entry locations, missing entry for unknown symbols and size failures and init text of settled modules and failed module holds, oversize for excessive return data, and not supported for disabled return builds. Pointer encoded errors distinguish resolution failures from null absence.
